### B384432 — The ledger bridge SEEDED A GENERATED FILE FROM ONE SIDE and dropped 48 of main's MAP.md descriptions `[Infra / CI]` (bug) #infra #testing  *(found 2026-08-13 while unsticking PR #978 on the owner's instruction — the bridge's FIRST outing on a PR it did not author, which is exactly what he asked it to be tested as. Minted **B384432** from this branch's reserved block B384432–B384447 against freshly-fetched `origin/main` 651849d. DEDUPE-FIRST — searched Open / ⏳ Verify / Done across `resolve-ledgers`, `B296224`, `MAP.md`, `build-map`, `--ours`, `checkout --ours`, `generated`, `doc-pointer`, `mapDrift`, `B779`, `B780`, `B290251`: **net-new, and deliberately NOT a B296224 recurrence.** B296224 is the CONFLICT RATE and its bridge is the remedy; this is a data-loss defect INSIDE that shipped remedy, in the half — the generated pair — that B296224's own text called the part that "cannot be got wrong by concatenation". Net-new.)*
`[x]` **✅ DONE 2026-08-13 — a generated file is now regenerated from a seed built out of BOTH merge sides, so no side's preserved, hand-authored content can be dropped. `Verify: sandbox`.**
- Verify: sandbox — a merge-resolution script with no runtime surface; the unit suite plus the live PR #978 measurement is the whole proof.
- Origin: found 2026-08-13 while carrying out the owner's ITEM 2 ("use the bridge and report whether it works"); fixed the same session.
- **⛔ THE DEFECT IN ONE LINE: "GENERATED" WAS READ AS "FULLY DERIVED", AND IT IS NOT.** Step 3 of the bridge ran `git checkout --ours` on `BACKLOG_OPEN.md` and `MAP.md` before regenerating them. `BACKLOG_OPEN.md` really is a pure function of `BACKLOG.md`, so the seed is irrelevant there. **`MAP.md` is not** — it carries a hand-authored one-line responsibility per path, and `build-map.mjs` PRESERVES those by parsing the copy already on disk. Seeding that parse from ONE side therefore discards every description the other side wrote.
- **THE MEASUREMENT, on a real PR rather than a constructed case.** PR #978 had sat four days; the test-merge against `main` was the pure ledger-only pattern the bridge was built for — `BACKLOG_OPEN.md` and `MAP.md` the only two conflicts, `BACKLOG.md` / `VERIFICATION.md` / `SitePlanner.jsx` / the tests all auto-merging, **zero source conflicts**. The bridge ran and reported `✅ Resolved 0 ledger file(s) … MAP.md (regenerated)`. **`node scripts/build-map.mjs --check` then went RED: 48 files that `main` describes came back as `TODO — describe`.** A merge the bridge had just declared resolved would have gone red in CI, and the 48 one-liners another session wrote would have been silently gone — which is the precise failure the script's own header says it exists to be incapable of.
- **THE FIX: `seedGenerated()` — the seed is BOTH SIDES CONCATENATED, theirs then ours.** Correct because the generator rebuilds the file from a FRESH SCAN and reads the seed only for its preserved-content map, keyed by path, so a path appearing twice costs nothing. Order is theirs-then-ours because that map is last-write-wins: a path both sides describe keeps OURS, the branch's own wording for its own file. `seedSide()` strips conflict markers and drops `TODO — describe` lines, so an undescribed side cannot clobber a described one. When the stages are gone (already staged, or a re-run) it recovers the two sides from `HEAD` / `MERGE_HEAD` instead of quietly seeding from a half-written file.
- **⛔ THE DISTINCTION THAT MUST SURVIVE: the seed is an INPUT to the generator, never the committed output.** Concatenation is safe precisely because nothing concatenated is kept — pinned by a test, since conflating the two is how a `MAP.md` with every path listed twice would get committed.
- **Sandbox evidence.** `test/resolveLedgers.test.js` **17 green** (+5): the one-side-only description (the PR #978 loss, directly), the TODO-clobber case, the ours-wins ordering, marker stripping, and the seed-is-not-output guard. **The mutation proof is the field measurement itself** — the pre-fix code was run against the real PR #978 merge and produced the 48-description loss above; the post-fix seed regenerates `MAP.md` at **505 files, 0 awaiting a description**, and `--check` passes.
- **PR #978's own merge was resolved with the corrected seed**, and its tree came out byte-identical to the resolution a concurrent session pushed independently — an accidental but real cross-check.
- **⛔ AND THE FIX ALONE WAS NOT ENOUGH — the PROPERTY is now asserted at runtime under `B384433`.** This item corrected the seed; nothing stopped it regressing silently. B384433 adds the post-condition (`lostDescriptions`) that REFUSES a run which comes back with fewer described paths, mutation-proven against the real PR #978 sides at 48-lost-before / 0-lost-after.
- Files: `scripts/resolve-ledgers.mjs`, `test/resolveLedgers.test.js`.
